cleanIntro: This guide follows Walther's PDP F-Series manual. That book covers the F-Series line and never names the Steel Frame, so check your pistol against it at every step. The book describes a polymer frame and lists only 3.5" and 4" barrels. Its slide comes apart as one section, its extractor pin turns 90 degrees with a screwdriver instead of drifting straight through, and its recoil spring assembly goes back in opposite ways depending on barrel length.

steps.title: This guide follows Walther's PDP F-Series book: check your pistol against it
steps.action: This guide follows Walther's PDP F-Series manual, which covers the F-Series line and does not name the Steel Frame, so check your pistol against it. The book's specification table lists two barrels only: 3.5" (89 mm) and 4" (102 mm). Read your own barrel length now and note it.
steps.prose: The book's two barrel lengths field strip identically but do not reassemble identically, and the book gives no orientation for any other length. If your barrel is neither length, the book does not tell you which way round your recoil spring assembly goes, so note exactly how it sits before it comes out and refit it the same way. Where your pistol differs from the one in the book's figures, follow the book only as far as it describes what you are holding.
steps.aside: The book describes a glass fibre reinforced polymer frame. It gives no care instruction specific to a steel frame.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL PDP F-SERIES PISTOLS — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — 6 Technical Specifications, printed p.26 (PDF p.26)

steps.title: Magazine out, then rack and lock open
steps.action: Finger off the trigger and outside the guard, muzzle safe, press the magazine release and remove the magazine. Then grip the rear slide serrations, draw the slide fully rearward in one brisk stroke, and let it ease forward slightly while pressing up on the slide stop so it locks open.
steps.prose: Put the magazine well out of reach of the bench, because the strip ends in a trigger press. The rack must be brisk and complete; a tentative stroke lets the extractor drag the case back rather than throwing it. Do not cover the ejection port with the supporting hand while you do it. The slide stop is easier to engage if you let the slide creep forward a few millimetres from its rearmost point first.
steps.quote: Lock the slide in the open position by allowing the slide to move slightly forward from the rearmost position while pressing upward on the slide stop (3.1 Figure 3).
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL PDP F-SERIES PISTOLS — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — 3.1 Inspecting the Pistol, printed p.10 (PDF p.10)

steps.title: Chamber, magazine well and bore — all three
steps.action: With the slide locked open, verify the chamber is unloaded, look down through the empty magazine well, and check the bore visually that it is clean, dry and free of any obstruction.
steps.prose: Read the chamber itself rather than trusting an indicator — solvent and residue hide what you are looking for. The bore check earns its place on a pistol that may have been stored oiled: oil standing in a bore raises pressure the next time it is fired. Run a finger into the chamber if the light is bad. Walther requires this whole sequence every time the pistol changes hands, is transported, is stored or is cleaned.
steps.quote: Check the chamber to verify that it is unloaded and check the bore visually that it is clean, dry, and free from any obstructions (3.1 Figure 4).
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL PDP F-SERIES PISTOLS — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — 3.1 Inspecting the Pistol, printed p.10 (PDF p.10)
steps.warn: Never rely on mechanical features alone. Walther's line is that the safety of the firearm rests on your handling of it.

steps.title: Muzzle safe, trigger fully to the rear
steps.action: Close the slide by pulling it slightly rearward and releasing it slowly. Point the pistol in a safe direction and squeeze the trigger fully to the rear.
steps.prose: In the book's sequence this press comes before the take-down catch, so treat it as part of the strip, not a convention. It is also the moment a live round left in the chamber discharges. Inspect both the chamber and the magazine well immediately beforehand — do both, in that order, with the muzzle still pointed somewhere safe.
steps.quote: Point the pistol in a safe direction. Squeeze the trigger fully to the rear.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL PDP F-SERIES PISTOLS — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — 4.1.1 Field-Stripping Disassembly, printed p.15 (PDF p.15)
steps.warn: To complete disassembly you will be required to pull the trigger. Inspect the chamber and the magazine well to be sure they are empty before your finger moves.

steps.title: Take-down catch down, slide off the front
steps.action: Grip the take-down catch from above, one finger each side, press it straight down, and hold it there while you run the slide forward off the frame.
steps.prose: Both sides must be loaded together or the catch cants in its slot and refuses to move — pressing harder on one side achieves nothing. Approaching from above keeps your hand behind the muzzle line while the slide travels forward. Once the catch drops, the slide leaves the rails with little resistance and there is nothing to arrest it, so keep hold of it.
steps.quote: Move the slide forward, and remove it from the frame.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL PDP F-SERIES PISTOLS — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — 4.1.1 Field-Stripping Disassembly, printed p.15 (PDF p.15)

steps.title: Recoil assembly out, barrel out — and note which way round it sat
steps.action: Turn the slide over, lift the recoil guide rod assembly out from under the barrel while taking up the spring pressure, then lift the barrel from the slide. Note which end of the recoil assembly sat at the muzzle.
steps.prose: The assembly is loaded, so ease the rear end out of the barrel recess rather than pulling it — pull and the spring flicks it out of your hand. Noting the orientation now matters more on this pistol than on the book's own, because the book's orientation rule is written for two barrel lengths only. The barrel then lifts straight out. You should have four parts: frame, slide, barrel, recoil spring assembly.
steps.quote: Remove the recoil guide rod assembly from below the barrel while taking up the spring pressure (4.1.1 Figure 2).
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL PDP F-SERIES PISTOLS — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — 4.1.1 Field-Stripping Disassembly, printed p.15 (PDF p.15)

steps.title: The book's recoil spring orientation depends on barrel length
steps.action: Before you put anything back: the book says on a 3.5" pistol the LARGER end of the recoil spring assembly goes into the spring mounting at the front of the slide, and on a 4" pistol the SMALLER end of the recoil rod goes into that mounting. If your barrel is neither length, refit the assembly exactly as you noted it came out.
steps.prose: The book gives two orientations, keyed to its two barrel lengths, and none for any other. Fitting it the wrong way round will feel almost right and will bind the slide, which reads as a gritty rail or a short-stroking gun rather than as an assembly error. Flex in the assembly as it seats is normal, so do not take flex as evidence you have it right. If you did not note the orientation and your barrel is not one of the book's two, stop and get it confirmed before firing.
steps.quote: Insert the recoil spring assembly: 3.5” pistol models: Insert the larger end of the recoil spring assembly into the spring mounting at the front of the slide. 4” pistol models: Place the smaller end of the recoil rod into the spring mounting at the front of the slide.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL PDP F-SERIES PISTOLS — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — 4.1.2 Field-Stripping Reassembly, printed p.15 (PDF p.15)
steps.warn: The book's orientation rule covers 3.5" and 4" barrels only. Read the barrel length off your own pistol.

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Frame, slide, barrel and recoil spring assembly. That is the book's published field strip; the slide assembly, the magazine and the preventive spring replacement are the deeper procedures.
steps.prose: Check the set against the main-components figure before any solvent is opened. From here the routine clean covers the bore from the chamber end, the breech face, the chamber end of the barrel, the extractor and adjacent surfaces, and the frame — the parts a range session actually fouls. The striker channel stays out of it because it takes no lubricant. The book's slide procedure is section 4.2 and it needs 1 mm and 2 mm drift punches plus a screwdriver.
steps.quote: The main components of the pistol are shown in 4.1.1 Figure 3.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL PDP F-SERIES PISTOLS — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — 4.1.1 Field-Stripping Disassembly, printed p.15 (PDF p.15)

deepSteps.title: End cap: punch, about 1.5 mm of travel, then pull it down
deepSteps.action: Stand the slide on its muzzle on a smooth flat surface and grip it at the rear serrations. Push a 2 mm drift punch in against the spring pressure through the round opening of the slide end cap, and while keeping downward pressure, slide the end cap down about 1.5 mm. Put the punch down and pull the end cap the rest of the way out. Then hold the safety plunger down and remove the striker assembly and its retract spring.
deepSteps.prose: The book's end cap comes off in two movements rather than one — a short shift while the punch holds the spring, then a straight pull once the punch is out. Trying to do it in a single stroke is what makes it feel seized. The spring behind it is live, so keep the slide standing on its muzzle and a hand over the cap throughout. If your slide's end cap does not match the book's figure, stop here.
deepSteps.quote: Push the safety plunger all the way down to the stop. While applying downward pressure on the safety plunger, remove the striker assembly and striker retract spring from the slide
deepSteps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL PDP F-SERIES PISTOLS — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — 4.2.1 Slide Disassembly, printed p.16 (PDF p.16)
deepSteps.warn: The striker assembly and its retract spring are under load. Hold the safety plunger down and control both as they come out.

deepSteps.title: Extractor pin turns 90 degrees — it does not drift straight out
deepSteps.action: Optic-ready models: take the cover or base plate off first. Hold the slide with the muzzle to the left and turn the extractor pin 90 degrees with a screwdriver into its disassembly position, so the slot in the pin lies perpendicular to the barrel.
deepSteps.prose: Reaching for a punch here will simply mar the pin. In the book the pin is keyed: until its slot is perpendicular to the barrel it is locked in the slide and no amount of drifting will move it. Turn it with a screwdriver blade that actually fills the slot, and check the orientation by eye before going further. If your extractor pin has no slot, your slide is not the book's, and you stop.
deepSteps.quote: Use a screwdriver to turn the extractor pin by 90° to the disassembly position (4.2.1 Fig. 3). The orientation of the extractor pin’s slot must be perpendicular to the barrel.
deepSteps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL PDP F-SERIES PISTOLS — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — 4.2.1 Slide Disassembly, printed p.16 (PDF p.16)

deepSteps.title: 1 mm punch from the top, thumb on the extractor
deepSteps.action: Insert a 1 mm drift punch from the top into the small hole at the top of the slide, turn the slide upside down and hold the extractor in place with your thumb, then carefully drift the 1 mm punch in to force the extractor pin outwards.
deepSteps.prose: One millimetre is a fragile punch and the hole is a close fit, so keep it square to the slide and drive it gently — a bent punch left in that hole is a much worse problem than a dirty extractor. Your thumb on the extractor is doing real work: the extractor is sprung and will pivot out the moment the pin clears. Once the pin starts to emerge, stop punching and pull it. Watch for the small spring as the extractor's rear end pivots clear.
deepSteps.quote: Carefully drift a 1 mm punch in (4.2.1 Fig. 4) to force the extractor pin outwards.
deepSteps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL PDP F-SERIES PISTOLS — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — 4.2.1 Slide Disassembly, printed p.16 (PDF p.16)
deepSteps.warn: The book's extractor carries a torsion spring. It will fly out if the extractor is released unsupported.

deepSteps.title: The extractor spring comes out
deepSteps.action: Remove the extractor spring from its seat inside the extractor slot, and keep it with the torsion spring and the safety plunger.
deepSteps.prose: The book directs you to take this spring out, so the slot can be cleaned properly. Lay the parts out in removal order — safety plunger and its spring, extractor, torsion spring, extractor spring — because reassembly runs safety first, then extractor, then striker.
deepSteps.quote: Remove the extractor spring from its seat inside the extractor slot (4.2.1 Fig. 5, #3).
deepSteps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL PDP F-SERIES PISTOLS — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — 4.2.1 Slide Disassembly, printed p.16 (PDF p.16)

deepSteps.title: Reassembly order inside the slide is fixed
deepSteps.action: Put the slide back together in this order: striker safety and its plunger first, then the extractor with its torsion spring, then the striker assembly. Do not try to seat the striker before the extractor is in.
deepSteps.prose: The parts interfere with one another, so an order that feels arbitrary is actually mechanical. Secure the safety plunger's spring in the plunger hole with a little gun lube, never grease, to stop it falling out while you work. When the safety is assembled correctly it sits slightly below the feed rib next to it; if it stands proud, it has not entered the deepest part of its blind hole. Check that before anything else goes in.
deepSteps.caution: Use gun lube, not grease, to hold the safety plunger spring in place. Grease will stay there and gum the plunger.
deepSteps.quote: Reassembly starts with the striker safety and the extractor, continue with the striker assembly.
deepSteps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL PDP F-SERIES PISTOLS — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — 4.2.2 Slide Reassembly, note, printed p.17 (PDF p.17)

deepSteps.title: Prove the striker is home before the end cap goes on
deepSteps.action: With the safety plunger at rest, try to pull the striker assembly back out of the slide. If it comes, it is not seated. Only when it will not come out do you align its guide with the striker channel and press it home with the end cap.
deepSteps.prose: This is a real test with a definite answer, and it is the only thing standing between a correctly assembled slide and one that will not fire. Align both tabs of the striker assembly, slide the retract spring onto the striker's front end, and insert with both noses facing up while holding the safety down; then release the safety plunger and pull. A striker that slides back out has caught on the safety rather than passing under it. Reinsert the end cap from the bottom of the slide until it snaps.
deepSteps.quote: The striker assembly is correctly seated if it can no longer be pulled out of the slide while the safety plunger is in its resting position.
deepSteps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL PDP F-SERIES PISTOLS — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — 4.2.2 Slide Reassembly, printed p.18 (PDF p.18)

deepSteps.title: Magazine strip
deepSteps.action: Depress the floorplate catch through the hole in the floorplate with a 4 mm drift punch, slide the floorplate forward off the tube while keeping the catch down, remove the catch and spring through the bottom, then turn the tube upright and take the follower out.
deepSteps.prose: Keep a thumb across the floorplate as it starts to move — the catch is the only thing restraining the magazine spring. On the book's +2 magazine the sequence starts differently: find the metal tab at the rear base and, with the floorplate fully seated rearward, push it toward the top of the magazine with a flat screwdriver until it protrudes from the base, then slide the floorplate as normal. Everything goes back in exactly the orientation it came out and nothing needs force. If a part will not go, it is round the wrong way.
deepSteps.quote: Turn the tube right side up and remove the follower through the bottom of the tube.
deepSteps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL PDP F-SERIES PISTOLS — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — 4.3.1 Magazine Disassembly, printed p.18 (PDF p.18)
deepSteps.warn: The magazine spring is under pressure. Control the floorplate catch and the spring while removing the floorplate.

deepSteps.title: 10,000 rounds: springs get replaced, not just cleaned
deepSteps.action: At about 10,000 shots, replace the recoil spring assembly, the striker retract spring and the mainspring. Field strip, remove the safety plunger then the striker assembly, take the retract spring off, and change the mainspring off the striker guide.
deepSteps.prose: The book gives these springs a service life, and running past it shows up as inconsistent ejection and the odd light strike long before anything breaks. To change the mainspring: stand the striker tip on a wooden or plastic base, keep the rear of the mainspring compressed, grasp the striker guide by its protruding projection and pivot that projection up until the guide comes off. The guide is reusable and goes back only one way — indentations on the outer edge of the rear end, flat at the muzzle end. Press it on without canting until it engages.
deepSteps.quote: After 10,000 shots, it is recommended to replace the recoil spring assembly, the retract spring and mainspring.
deepSteps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL PDP F-SERIES PISTOLS — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — 4.7 Preventive Maintenance, printed p.21 (PDF p.21)

deepSteps.title: Striker channel dry, one drop everywhere else
deepSteps.action: Clean and dry the striker channel and put no gun lubricant into it. In the slide, one drop on surface (E) and one on the safety plunger (F); on the frame, one drop on each slide guide and one on the trigger bar.
deepSteps.prose: Lubricate from the book's own diagram, surface (E) and the safety plunger (F). Oil in the striker channel collects powder and carbon and slows the striker until primers dent rather than fire, which reads as an ammunition fault. A light film on the barrel's external surfaces and on the ramp where the locking block cams it. Magazines take a film on external metal surfaces only.
deepSteps.caution: Do not put any gun lubricant into the striker channel. Over-lubricating anywhere attracts dirt, unburned powder and carbon residue.
deepSteps.quote: Slide: Put only one drop of lubricant on surface (E) and the safety plunger (F).
deepSteps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL PDP F-SERIES PISTOLS — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — 4.5 Lubrication, printed p.20 (PDF p.20)

cleaning.name: BARREL & CHAMBER
tasks: Brush from the CHAMBER end until the bristles fully exit at the muzzle, then pull back until they fully exit the chamber end — no reversing inside the bore
Powder-removing solvent and a brass bristle bore brush to lift lead and firing residue out of the barrel
Wipe clean with patches or a swab, then a light film of gun lubricant on the barrel's external surfaces and on the ramp where the locking block cams it
Threaded-barrel guns: clean and re-check the thread and refit the thread protector before storage

cleaning.name: SLIDE, BREECH FACE & EXTRACTOR
tasks: Small brush in solvent around the breech face, the chamber end of the barrel, the extractor and the adjacent areas exposed to powder or primer residue
One drop of lubricant on slide surface (E) and one on the safety plunger (F), per the book's diagram
Striker channel DRY: no lubricant at any point
Optic-ready models: refit the cover or base plate before the slide is cycled

cleaning.name: FRAME & RAILS
tasks: Light brushing with solvent to lift residue off the frame
One drop of lubricant on each slide guide and one on the trigger bar
Light film of high quality gun lubricant on all external metal surfaces, then wipe clean
Cold climate: use a lubricant that will not congeal at low temperature

cleaning.name: MAGAZINES
tasks: Light film of gun lubricant on external metal surfaces only
Wipe the tube interior dry; oil inside collects grit and drags the follower
Inspect the feed lips and follower while the magazine is apart, and never use excessive force reassembling it
+2 magazines: hold the tab flush with the body while sliding the floorplate fully rearward, then push the tab into its correct seating

cleaning.name: SOLVENT LIMITS & SERVICE LIFE
tasks: No ammonia-based or strong alkaline solvents on any Walther firearm
Avoid prolonged solvent immersion and prolonged ultrasonic cleaning; 50 °C (122 °F) is the ultrasonic ceiling
Log the round count — recoil spring assembly, retract spring and mainspring are replacement items at about 10,000 shots
Check the pistol for signs of wear every time it is cleaned; if wear is noted, stop using it and have it checked

reassembly: Slide upside down, barrel in with the locking lugs oriented as the manual's figure shows.

Recoil spring assembly: the book says LARGER end into the spring mounting at the front of the slide on 3.5" models, SMALLER end of the recoil rod on 4" models. Any other barrel length: refit it exactly as it came out.
Insert the rear end of the spring assembly into the lower barrel recess while compressing the spring. Flex in the assembly is normal.
Push the slide onto the frame from the front until the take-down catch engages, checking the slide has also picked up the rear slide guides, then release it fully forward into the locked position.

If the slide was opened: striker safety and plunger first, then extractor with its torsion spring and the extractor spring, then the striker assembly — and prove the striker will not pull back out before the end cap goes on.
Turn the extractor pin back with a screwdriver until its slot lies slightly toward the muzzle; pressing the extractor in repeatedly helps it orientate.
Magazine back together in original orientation, floorplate on until the catch snaps audibly.
Dry-patch the bore before the pistol is loaded.
fncheck: Magazine out, chamber confirmed empty: rack the slide and let it run — it must return fully into battery unaided, with no grit or hesitation on the rails (a wrongly oriented recoil spring assembly shows up exactly here). Lock it open on the slide stop and drop it with the thumb. Insert the empty magazine and pull down on the floorplate; it should not move. If the slide was opened, confirm the striker assembly cannot be pulled out with the safety plunger at rest, that the safety sits slightly below the feed rib beside it, and that the extractor springs back flush when pressed. Optic-ready guns: cover or base plate fitted and tight before the pistol is fired.
